subject: Service escrow and prioritization ladders for premium support
messages:
From: Lara Holt <lara.holt@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2027-03-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Inquiry: SLA tiers + escalation coverage for a potential Dedicated deployment

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Acme liked the throughput profile. Before we get legal involved, procurement asked me to confirm upfront how Redwood structures premium support for Dedicated customers. High level we care about:

- Uptime guarantees (we're targeting 99.95% across API endpoints)
- Response / incident triage SLAs (P1/P2 windows and RTO expectations)
- Escalation coverage (on-call roster, third-line engagement, regional overlap)
- Credits / remediation formula for outages
- Any retainer/retainer refund/retainer-for-support models you offer

Can you share a pricing sketch and the tradeoffs between: (a) a 12-month committed capacity + 10% discount, (b) a 24-month commit, and (c) a short-term pilot with an uptick surcharge? Also: do you offer a service-escrow or similar artifact for on-prem/dedicated customers? Procurement will want to see an example MAA/SLA and a sample escalation roster.

Appreciate a concise breakdown. If useful we can jump on a 30-min call this week.

Thanks,
Lara Holt
Director, Platform Operations
Acme Systems
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lara Holt <lara.holt@acme.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-08T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SLA tiers + escalation coverage for a potential Dedicated deployment

Hi Lara — great to hear Acme liked the demo. High-level proposal below; attaching a short SLA draft and a scoping sheet so procurement has something concrete to review.

Attachments: SLA_Draft_20270308.pdf (draft), MAA-scoping-sheet.xlsx (scoping)

Summary (short):
- Uptime tiers: 99.9% (Standard), 99.95% (Enhanced), 99.99% (Premium). Pricing delta driven by reserved GPU capacity and regional failover slots.

- Response windows:
  - P1 (system-wide outage): 15-minute phone acknowledgement, on-call engineer routed within 30 minutes, 4-hour remediation SLO for failover-based recovery; creditable events computed as % of daily uptime below target.
  - P2 (severe degradation): 1-hour response, 8-business-hour remediation target.
  - P3 (functional bug / feature request): 1 business day acknowledgement, SLAs for planned work per roadmap.

- Escalation coverage:
  - Standard: regional business-hours triage + 24/7 paging for P1 incidents
  - Enhanced: named SE + extended regional on-call overlap (APAC/US/EU) during your maintenance windows
  - Premium: 24/7 named escalation ring with guaranteed third-line engagement within 2 hours and monthly operational reviews; includes an on-call retainer option.

- Credits: we use an uptime-credit slab: 99.95–99.99 = 5% monthly credit; 99.9–99.95 = 10%; <99.9 = 20% (applied to monthly Dedicated service fee). We can discuss heavier remediation for multi-day outages.

- Retainer models:
  - No retainer: standard coverage as above; credits apply automatically.
  - Fixed retainer: charged monthly to guarantee named SE and faster escalation windows (applies to Enhanced/Premium). Retainer offsets credits up to a cap.
  - Escrow: for Dedicated/on-prem customers we can provide a limited service-escrow (config + deployment recipe, access gating) under a separate agreement; good for regulated customers.

Pricing sketch (illustrative):
- 12-month commit: base price X, Enhanced uptime +10% on base, 10% volume discount available for committed GPU hours.
- 24-month commit: base price X - 7%, Enhanced uptime same premium, 12% volume discount and waived implementation retainer.
- Pilot (3 months): 20% uplift on hourly rates, no volume discount, limited SLA (99.9%) until commit transitions to Dedicated contract.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Decide which uptime tier you want to anchor (Enhanced 99.95% is common for workloads with low-latency SLAs).
2) I’ll route a short MAA/SLA and a pricing term sheet to procurement — the attached draft can be adapted.
3) If you want, Vanessa (cc'd) can map this to our Dedicated SKUs and run a quick impact on pricing for the commit sizes you mentioned.

Happy to jump on a call today 1–3pm PT if that helps.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lara Holt <lara.holt@acme.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-08T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SLA tiers + escalation coverage for a potential Dedicated deployment

Thanks Irene — jumping in with SKU-level guidance. Lara, quick notes from pricing ops: 

- For a 12-month commit: we typically layer a 10% committed discount on top of the Enhanced uptime premium, plus a 5% onboarding credit if you sign within 30 days.
- For 24 months: we can move to a blended 12%–15% discount depending on committed GPU-hours and whether you prepay.
- Pilot path: recommend a 6-week pilot (shorter than 3 months) with an implementation retainer that is fully credited if you convert to a 12-month commit. Pilot rates carry a 15–20% uplift.

Operational asks: please confirm expected monthly token throughput and your primary region (us-east/us-west/eu-west) — those two inputs materially change reserved capacity sizing and pricing. HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2027-001

I'll include the standard escalation roster template in the final pricing packet.

- Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lara Holt <lara.holt@acme.com>
Date: 2027-03-08T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SLA tiers + escalation coverage for a potential Dedicated deployment

Looping in a couple of practical negotiation points from the sales team: Lara — appreciate the clarity. Two asks we typically see that affect commercial structuring: 

1) Escalation ring composition: if Acme wants third-party SE engagement (e.g., a partner-managed observability layer), we prefer to add a short SOW for triage rather than bake that into the base SLA. If you'd like, we can include an optional Partner SE line item in the quote.

2) Credit formula clarity: is Acme OK with a monthly credit slab (Irene's proposal) or do you prefer per-incident credits with lookback windows? Per-incident is sometimes requested by finance for visibility into root-cause.

Counterproposal on discounts: we can offer a stepped volume discount: 8% for commits up to Y hours, 12% for commits > Y and < Z, and 18% for > Z (numbers to be populated after you share throughput). This avoids heavy upfront concessions and aligns to usage.

If you confirm throughput and region Vanessa asked about, I can turn this into a concrete commercial proposal and draft SOW for the Partner SE option.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Lara Holt <lara.holt@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SLA tiers + escalation coverage for a potential Dedicated deployment

Irene/Vanessa/Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clarity. We reviewed the draft with our platform and finance teams overnight. Quick answers: 

- Region: primary region will be us-east, occasional failover to eu-west.
- Estimated monthly throughput: ~1.4B tokens (rough summer baseline, headroom expected).
- We prefer per-incident credits with a 30-day RCA lookback for major outages.
- We are open to the Partner SE SOW as a line item; please include as optional.

Next steps for us: procurement wants an updated MAA with the per-incident credit language, the Partner SE SOW as optional, and the stepped discount banding Ben described. If you can produce an updated packet and DocuSign-ready MAA by Friday, we'll aim to turn this into a 12-month commit with a 10% target discount.

I'll send a procurement contact if you need an official PO template. Thanks again — would appreciate a 30-min call on Friday morning PT to finalize items.

Best,
Lara Holt
Director, Platform Operations
Acme Systems
[Procurement: procurement@acme.com]
